ai.title: addsubgoal schema gains log field
ai.summary: The `add_subgoal` tool schema in `common/src/constants/tools.ts` now accepts a `log` field, aligning with `update_subgoal`. This ensures subgoal creation can capture initial log entries directly, matching the update workflow. Scope limited to shared core tool definitions.

eli5.text: When the assistant creates a new step in a goal, you can now give that step an initial log note right away instead of only being able to add or change notes later. The create-step feature and the edit-step feature now ask for the same details, so tracking information stays consistent from the moment a step is added. Because this just updates the data format the assistant uses, nothing looks different yet until the assistant is taught to fill in that log field.

ai.title: Skip request files only when prompt empty
ai.summary: Changed `skipRequestingFiles` logic in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to `!prompt` instead of `justUsedATool`. This ensures file context requests are skipped only when no user prompt is provided, rather than based on tool usage history.

eli5.text: When the assistant starts up, it will no longer ask you to share files with it unless there's actually a message from you. In other words, if you don't provide a prompt, the file-request step is skipped; if you do provide a prompt, the assistant proceeds to request files as it normally would. You'd only notice this in the narrow case where you trigger the assistant with no input text, it previously still nudged you for file access even then, and now it won't. This is a minor backend tweak that's already live.

ai.title: Fix tool result ordering in main prompt
ai.summary: Refactors backend/src/main-prompt.ts to append tool results directly to message history before user prompts, eliminating intermediate arrays. This ensures correct chronological ordering of assistant responses and tool outputs for the LLM. Internal logic change only; no API or UI surface impact.

eli5.text: When you talk to the assistant and it uses tools (like reading files), the assistant's tool results and your next message now appear in the correct order instead of getting mixed up. This only affects how the assistant processes conversations internally; you won't see any difference in what's displayed.

ai.title: readfiles tool renderer updated to display trimmed content
ai.summary: The read_files tool renderer in npm-app/src/utils/tool-renderers.ts now uses defaultToolCallRenderer with custom handlers. onParamChunk returns null to suppress intermediate chunk rendering, while onParamEnd returns content.trim() to display the final file content. This change affects how file reading operations are visualized in the CLI and Web/Desktop tool output surfaces.

eli5.text: When the assistant reads a file's contents to show you, it now waits until the full content is in hand and displays it without extra surrounding text or spacing. You will see the file contents appear cleanly formatted instead of as they come in piece by piece with possible extra whitespace. This affects what you see when the assistant reads files in the app, and it is live today.

ai.title: Bump npm-app version to 1.0.191
ai.summary: Version bump in npm-app/package.json from 1.0.190 to 1.0.191. Internal release increment. Scope: npm-app package only.

eli5.text: The assistant's version number was bumped from 1.0.190 to 1.0.191 as part of a routine internal release. This update includes several small improvements: the spinning loader no longer gets stuck during certain tasks, a new logging feature was added to help track sub-goals, file requests are handled more intelligently, tool results appear in the correct order in prompts, and file content is displayed more cleanly. If you use the assistant today, you might notice smoother loading and more organized output, though the changes are subtle and mainly polish how existing features behave.

ai.title: Soften git command restrictions in main prompt
ai.summary: The `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` guideline for git and script execution was softened from prohibiting actions without specific instructions to requiring specific requests. The updated text adds a rationale about preventing costly accidents and explicitly states that the user is in charge, instructing the agent not to refuse user requests. This change applies to the core system prompt logic.

eli5.text: If you ask the assistant to run a git command or script, it can now go ahead without needing a special follow-up instruction first. Before this change, the assistant would hold back unless it got a very specific, separate request to proceed; now it waits for your direct ask and then acts, with a note that stopping it from helping could cause more harm than letting it run. This applies immediately to anyone giving instructions to the assistant today.
